text: This is PneumoScreen: a low-cost aid that helps community health workers spot pneumonia in young children.
The health worker signs in to the screening app.
They connect the Bluetooth sensor device. The app shows which sensors are working, and what the device's own screen says.
Next, they choose the child. The child's age sets the World Health Organization fast-breathing threshold, and the worker checks for danger signs.
The device rests on the belly and counts every breath, with a large countdown the worker can read at arm's length.
A thermometer reading is added. Fever is flagged at thirty-eight degrees.
Then the microphone records lung sounds at four chest positions. The A.I. model runs on the phone itself. If a recording is too noisy, the app asks to record it again.
Finally, the app combines everything into one clear result: normal, refer, or danger. And it saves the screening to the clinic server.
At the clinic, supervisors follow every screening and every recording, and see which children need follow-up.
